title: Sector-specific CII categorization overlay for banking and other financial-market spheres

act.effective_date_note: The act states no special commencement rule; 2026-02-15 is derived from first official publication on 2026-02-07 and the general seven-day rule.

governance_rules.rule: Defines sector-specific establishment and calculation of significance indicators for financial-market CII objects.
Categorization must account for sector specifics and current statutory lists of typical sector CII objects.

Defines covered public bodies and financial-market legal persons and identifies lawful-system ownership or operation; system presence is evidenced by resource and industrial-system inventory, financial records and commissioning documents.
Categorization uses PP 127 base rules and this overlay together.

Changes to typical-object or significance-indicator lists trigger review under PP 127; changed categories are sent to FSTEC under PP 127, then current significant-object information is sent to the clause-35 recipient.
Annually provide the current significant-object list plus the decision to review or not review categories based on the previous calendar year's assessment.
The subject head creates a permanent categorization commission by organizational act and approves commission rules; additional persons may be included.
Categorize objects matching information-system types in the applicable typical-sector-object lists.

A newly created object outside the current type list is still categorized when possible consequences match significance values; send object data and a list-amendment proposal to FSTEC and the clause-35 recipient. Systems serving another sphere must be checked against that sphere's typical-object lists.
Use typical-object lists plus sections II and III of this overlay for indicator establishment.
Presence of the information-system type in a typical-sector-object list is a sector significance feature.
For an object outside the type lists whose consequences match significance values, calculate the significance indicator best fitting the identified object.

calculation_rules.rule: Calculate PP 127 indicators with the operating specifics of the financial-market CII object.
Assess non-performance of statutory public functions; for the Bank of Russia this is limited to money-transfer functions.
Assess treaty breach or disruption of negotiations or signing by treaty level.
Calculate under the subject's internal documents.

Select downtime or degradation time from applicable Bank of Russia operational-reliability requirements, payment-system or digital-ruble-platform requirements, or the subject's own maximum service-disruption time for other cases.

variables.C_max: Maximum annual subject contributions to Russian budget-system budgets over the last three years
variables.Y: Associated economic harm averaged over the last three years
variables.D: Forecast annual federal-budget revenue averaged over the planned three-year period

calculation_rules.rule: Average yearly maximum downtime/degradation over three years; if fewer than three years have elapsed, use the actual period and add later years until three years are accumulated.

For each calendar year use the maximum among the allowable cumulative time, the threshold allowable-time level and actual cumulative downtime/degradation over the preceding 12 calendar months when the allowable degradation share was exceeded.
Use the maximum annual contributions to Russian budget-system budgets over the last three years.
Average over three years the enumerated remediation, personnel, contractual, reputational and direct financial losses.
Forecast annual federal-budget revenue averaged over the planned three-year period.

calculation_rules.variable: Millions of money-transfer operations for the year, forecast for newly created objects.
Trillions of rubles of performed clearing money-transfer obligations over the last 12 months.
Thousands of Russian-issuer securities recorded at the central depository over the last 12 months.

calculation_rules.rule: Use worst-case targeted-attack scenarios, process and object dependencies, threat feasibility and prior incident statistics; do not silently credit existing controls, analogue instruments or paper fallback when estimating maximum possible harm.

guardrails: Do not route the overlay outside proven banking or financial-market subject and object facts.
Do not omit PP 127 or current typical-sector-object lists.
An object outside the current type list is not automatically out of scope; clauses 9 and 12 require consequence-based review.
The clause 5 ten-working-day period starts on receipt of FSTEC confirmation, not on the commission decision or submission to FSTEC.
The clause 6 annual due point is the tenth working day of the calendar year, not 10 calendar days and not January 10.
The tenth-working-day values in clauses 50 to 52 are measurement snapshots, not reporting deadlines.
Three-year and twelve-month periods in clauses 41 to 49 are calculation windows, not evidence-retention duties.
Clause 7 permits additional commission members but does not require a universal external member.
Clause 55 is expressly recommendatory and must not be promoted to an unconditional mandatory duty.
No category is proven until complete facts and the applicable PP 127 threshold comparison are documented.
